title: Analyzing Root Halotropism in Arabidopsis thaliana Using Split-Agar System
author: Yu, Zheng, et al.

steps.title: Prepare truncated ruler
steps.instruction: Cut a plastic ruler to ~14 cm (the diagonal of a 10 cm × 10 cm square Petri dish) and polish the cut edge before use.

steps.title: Prepare split‑agar plates with separator
steps.instruction: Create split‑agar plates using a sterilized plastic ruler as a diagonal separator.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of ½ MS medium (1.2 % agar, 1 % sucrose, pH 5.7) and a second 1 L of the same medium supplemented with 200 mM NaCl; autoclave both at 120 °C for 20 min.
Cool the NaCl‑containing medium on a magnetic stirrer to 45 °C and keep it in a 65 °C incubator until use.
Sterilize the truncated ruler with 75 % ethanol for 10 min, then place it along the diagonal of a 10 cm × 10 cm disposable square Petri dish.
Using a 1 mL pipette, seal the junction between ruler and dish with the 200 mM NaCl medium.
Allow the sealed side to solidify for 5 min, then pour additional 200 mM NaCl medium into that half of the dish.
After 20 min of solidification, carefully remove the plastic ruler.
Pour the ½ MS medium kept at 65 °C into the empty half of the dish (add any extra reagents here if desired).
Let the newly poured medium solidify (~15 min), then let the whole plate dry uncovered for 30–45 min.
Use the split‑agar plates within 6 h to limit Na⁺ diffusion.

steps.title: Prepare split‑agar plates by cutting medium
steps.instruction: Make split‑agar plates by solidifying a NaCl medium and removing half of it with a blade.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 L of ½ MS medium (1.2 % agar, 1 % sucrose, pH 5.7) and 1 L of the same medium containing 200 mM NaCl; autoclave both at 120 °C for 20 min.
Cool the NaCl‑containing medium on a magnetic stirrer to 45 °C and keep it in a 65 °C incubator.
Pour the 200 mM NaCl medium into a 10 cm × 10 cm disposable square Petri dish and let it solidify for ~20 min.
Using a sterile blade, cut the solidified medium diagonally.
Press the half‑medium inward along the dish–medium interface, then press it outward along the cut line to remove one half of the agar.
Pour the ½ MS medium kept at 65 °C into the empty half of the dish (add any additional reagents here if needed).
After the newly added medium solidifies for ~15 min, dry the plate uncovered for 30–45 min.
Use the split‑agar plates within 6 h to minimize Na⁺ diffusion.
